trust_decision.summary: Whether curl verifies the remote TLS peer certificate is decided in CurlClient::generateDefaultOptions: whenever ssl_allow_self_signed is truthy, CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER is set to $verifyPeer. That property has no default (null), so verification is off unless a caller passes ssl_verify_peer explicitly. SyncTool::setupHttpSocket decides which params to pass based on the server's self_signed/cert_file columns.

landing_point.why: The summary names CurlClient and peer verification; this is the only CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER write in the class, and it is fed by the uninitialised $verifyPeer at line 29.

fix_sites.entry_point: Every CurlClient construction: SyncTool::createHttpSocket (server sync pull/push/testConnection in app/Controller/ServersController.php:1111, app/Console/Command/ServerShell.php:196, Cerebrate, webhook/Splunk workflow modules, EventReport LLM) and Module::initHttpSocket (enrichment/Cortex modules, app/Model/Module.php:453)

SyncTool::setupHttpSocket, reached from server sync (AppModel::setupHttpSocket app/Model/AppModel.php:3974-3983, ServersController testConnection, ServerShell), Cerebrate (app/Model/Cerebrate.php:39) and workflow doRequest (app/Model/WorkflowModules/action/Module_webhook.php:179)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: app/Model/Module.php:442-457 builds a CurlClient on its own from Plugin.<family>_ssl_* config and never goes through SyncTool. Its `if ($value && ...)` filter at line 446 drops ssl_verify_peer=false/unset, so Cortex/enrichment with *_ssl_allow_self_signed=true lands on the null $verifyPeer. The CurlClient default closes it; a fix limited to SyncTool would leave it open.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver who fixes only SyncTool's param building can argue that enrichment/Cortex module sockets are a separate plugin feature with their own admin settings (app/Model/Server.php:8710-8733) and outside 'sync TLS'. For the O8 workflow routes they can argue that the self-signed/verify_tls options are explicit user choices in a neighbouring feature, not the CurlClient default.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A server with self_signed=1 and no pinned CA must keep connecting with verification off. After a CA is removed, cert_file is saved as '' (not null), so flipping the default to true without the SyncTool isset->empty change would verify against the system CA store and break that server. A server with self_signed=1 and a pinned CA must verify against that CA.

O6_input_shapes: cert_file '' (CA removed and saved): verify off after the fix
cert_file non-empty with self_signed: verify on against the pinned CA
ssl_verify_peer absent from params: CurlClient default now true
ssl_verify_peer explicitly false/true passed by the caller

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The Splunk HEC export workflow module reads $params inside sendToSplunk, where it is not defined, so self_signed is always true. setupHttpSocket then sets ssl_verify_peer=false explicitly, and TLS verification is off even when the user picks 'Verify HTTPS Certificate = True' (default 1).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Looks like an unrelated workflow-module scoping bug, and self_signed is a deliberate user option; it is not the CurlClient default.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The webhook workflow module falls back to allowing self-signed certificates when the self_signed param is missing (for example a node saved before the option existed), although the declared default is 'deny'. With no cert_file this explicitly turns peer verification off.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Backward-compatibility default for older saved workflows; the UI default (line 59) is already 'deny'.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Another package (app/Model/WorkflowModules/action); state comes from a saved workflow node

O8_uncovered_routes.route: CurlClient sets CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYHOST=0 whenever allowSelfSigned is truthy, even when a CA is pinned or the system store is used with verifyPeer true. It also ignores the ssl_verify_host param that Module.php and Sightingdb pass, so hostname checking is lost in self-signed mode.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Accepting self-signed certificates conventionally relaxes hostname matching, and the advisory says 'peer verification', not hostname.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: Same file as the landing point

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Set $verifyPeer = true (or always set CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER true) in CurlClient and stop. This breaks self-signed servers whose CA was removed (cert_file ''), and leaves the Splunk/webhook workflow routes passing verify_peer=false explicitly.
